No. 9323 and Ex. Ord. No. 10444 (Apr. 10, 1953, 18 F.R. 2069) and Ex. Ord. No. 14085 (section 2, Oct. 3, 2022, 87 F.R. 60541) in a note at 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. clauses.reason: The order restates Executive Order 8809 (as amended by 9323) as one paragraph establishing the Good Conduct Medal for exemplary behavior, efficiency and fidelity, with eligibility by three years of service from August 27, 1940, one year of wartime service after December 7, 1941, or shorter honorable service after June 27, 1950, and a proviso against awards for under one year except for service-incurred disability. Executive Order 14085 section 2 (87 FR 60541; no later effective date is stated, so the signing date October 3, 2022 is used) amended that restated text by striking men and inserting members and adding Space Force references on or after December 20, 2019; the amendment changes the persons covered but not the clause's continuation. No held instrument revokes or supersedes the order, the U.S. Code note still prints it as amended, and the order cites no authority statute that could lapse, so the clause is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Read the whole order (18 FR 2069, signed 1953-04-10; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10444.txt): it further amends Executive Order 8809 of June 28, 1941 (Good Conduct Medal), as amended by Executive Order 9323 of March 31, 1943, to read as a single restated paragraph, issued under the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief (no authority statute is cited). The restated text establishes the Good Conduct Medal for exemplary behavior, efficiency and fidelity under regulations the Secretary of the Army and the Secretary of the Air Force prescribe, for enlisted men of the Army and Air Force who on or after August 27, 1940 completed three years of active Federal military service, or served one year after December 7, 1941 while the United States is at war, or at the end of service had completed less than three years if any part was after June 27, 1950, with a proviso that no one except persons separated for physical disability incurred in line of duty receives it for under one year. The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes. later-events:ofr_catalog has 1 hit, the Office of the Federal Register note that this order amends EO 8809 (with a see-reference to EO 9323); that is the order's own effect on its parent, not a later event against it. current-law:usc has 1 hit: 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 note, which prints Ex. Ord. No. 8809 as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 9323, Ex. Ord. No. 10444 (Apr. 10, 1953, 18 F.R. 2069) and Ex. Ord. No. 14085 (section 2, Oct. 3, 2022, 87 F.R. 60541) with no ending statement (release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09). current-law:ecfr has 1 hit that is only a search lead and states no ending. The held text of Executive Order 14085 (87 FR 60541) section 2 amends Executive Order 8809 as amended by 9323 and 10444 by striking men and inserting members and by adding references to the Space Force on or after December 20, 2019 after the August 27, 1940, December 7, 1941 and June 27, 1950 dates; it is recorded as a later event, and under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended. The Federal Register issue of April 14, 1953 also prints Army and Air Force regulation notes (32 CFR 578.27 and 878.46, indexed by the packet as an EO 10445 item) whose editorial notes only refer to this order; they are not amendments or an end. The held-corpus search for the number 10444 found no revocation or supersession.

savings.reason: The order has no saving clause. It restates the parent order in full and issues no one-time command, so there is no pending-matter residue; the effect on Executive Order 8809 as amended by 9323 is that the restated paragraph replaces that text. The three bounded searches found no other residue or later instrument besides Executive Order 14085.
